title: SHRINE/25 — Nothing Left Behind
dek: The offering is attention. The proof is the clean close.
body:
SHRINE/25 proposes a local public shrine as a hosted interval of attention, not an unattended object or a claim on public land. It is temporary, attended, small enough to carry, and complete only when every person and object leaves.

Twelve protocols give the interval a shape: First Light, Wind Register, Water Thanks, The Best Seat, Repair Minute, Names Carried, Fair Start, Five Small Visits, Good Handoff, Ring Vigil, West Color, and Clean Close. Each specifies what to bring, one shared act, the close, and what never belongs. The object is not the shrine. The quality of attention is.

A private composer combines one of twenty-five official-source public doors, one protocol, one watch, and one company size. It produces a portable score and routes the idea through one of four reality lanes: pocket shrine, hosted gathering, built installation, or public event. Those are editorial operating distinctions, not legal advice or permission.

LA County says organized group activities on County-operated beaches and in Marina del Rey require a Special Event Use Permit; its examples include memorials, vendors, and setup of tables and chairs. County park events may require facility-use and additional review. Dockweiler fire belongs only in current designated rings under current rules. Formal public art follows the relevant owner or agency process.

The page requests no account, identity, geolocation, camera, microphone, cookies, analytics, or network write. The generated score stays in page memory unless the visitor explicitly presses Keep this score, which writes one documented browser-local key. Copy and erase are user-controlled. A short bell is gesture-started synthesis, not a recording.

This release is independent PointCast editorial. It does not announce, authorize, reserve, install, schedule, fund, host, or invite attendance to an event, memorial, installation, restoration, or public program. Current official sources, posted rules, staff direction, permits, access conditions, closures, fire conditions, and protected-area requirements control.
